paragraphs: Children in care from the city of Lincoln are looked after by Lincolnshire County Council's own fostering service and by the agencies shown above. The council says its in-house service was rated Outstanding by Ofsted in 2023. In March 2026 it said more foster carers were needed and asked residents for their views on fostering in the county.

The council says it has an urgent need for long-term carers, including for groups of brothers and sisters, and it also looks for parent and child carers and for carers of unaccompanied young people aged 15 to 17. Single people, LGBTQIA+ and disabled people, people in work or on benefits, and people who rent can all apply, with no upper age limit. You need a spare bedroom, couples need to have lived together for 18 months, and smokers cannot foster children under five.

Lincolnshire's route runs from an enquiry and home visit to an application, checks and references, a three-day preparation course, an assessment and the fostering panel. Its Caring2Learn programme continues with a first-year training pathway, and carers have a supervising social worker, a buddy and free membership of The Fostering Network.

Lincolnshire publishes its 2026-27 weekly allowance for each child, from £192.98 for a child up to four to £331.66 for a young person aged 16 and over, effective from 1 April 2026. It also pays retention bonuses of £500 after one year, £1,000 after five years and £2,000 after ten. Our Lincolnshire allowance page has the full table.
Our Lincolnshire page covers the county as a whole. Speak to the council's team and to two or three of the services above about the children they most need homes for and the support they give.
